entries.behavior: Across two clients under sustained large-object delete, put, get, and eviction pressure, every successful read returns the exact bytes most recently written for its key.
entries.reason: No discoverable Rust crate test currently sustains randomized cross-client delete/put/get operations with large values and eviction pressure.

entries.behavior: During repeated random crashes and restarts of a three-Master HA group, successful small-object puts remain readable with exact values, and service resumes for all keys after a surviving leader stabilizes.
entries.reason: No discoverable Rust crate test currently performs repeated randomized three-Master process crashes/restarts while asserting cross-client small-object availability and integrity.

entries.behavior: During repeated random crashes and restarts of a three-Master HA group under eviction-prone large-object pressure, every successful read preserves exact object bytes and stable surviving leaders resume service.
entries.reason: No discoverable Rust crate test currently combines randomized three-Master crash/restart cycles with large-object eviction pressure and cross-client byte-integrity assertions.

entries.behavior: An RPC bind host already expressed as a bare IPv4 address passes through unchanged and can start the RPC server.
entries.reason: Rust has segment-name routing normalization tests but no equivalent test that derives and binds the Client RPC host from a bare configured address.

entries.behavior: A configured IPv4 host with a data-plane port is stripped to the bare host before RPC server binding, allowing the server to start.
entries.reason: Rust has segment-name routing normalization tests but no equivalent assertion on Client RPC bind-host derivation and successful binding.

entries.behavior: Decimal and 0x/0X hexadecimal object keys parse as complete unsigned sequence hashes, while empty, malformed, and trailing-garbage keys are rejected.
A disabled KV-event publisher is a no-op for stored and removed notifications and leaves published and dropped counters at zero.
When the KV-event queue reaches capacity, the publisher drops the oldest event, retains newer events, and increments its dropped-event accounting.
Publishing an SGLang object key over ZMQ emits a three-frame message with sequence, stored event type, backend, tenant, group, object key, empty sequence hashes, and successful publish statistics.
Pinned-memory registration rejects duplicate and overlapping ranges while accepting an adjacent range, and each accepted range unregisters exactly once when released.
entries.reason: Rust implements overlap checks for owner-backed registrations but has no discoverable fake-native test proving duplicate/overlap rejection, adjacent acceptance, and exact unregister calls.

entries.behavior: Pinned-memory quota rejects capacity beyond the configured limit, releasing a region refunds capacity, and a later full-size registration succeeds and unregisters once.
entries.reason: Rust owner-backed registration has no equivalent configured pinned-byte quota test with release/refund accounting.

entries.behavior: A failed native pin operation refunds its reservation so retrying the same range after native recovery succeeds and later unregisters exactly once.
entries.reason: Rust has no discoverable fake-native regression test proving failed registration leaves no live or blocked reservation and permits an exact retry.

entries.behavior: A failed native unregister retains the address and quota reservation, preventing overlapping or capacity-consuming replacement registrations from reusing unsafe memory.
entries.reason: Rust records blocked ranges after Drop-time unregister failure, but no discoverable fake-native test proves the range remains unavailable after the failure.

entries.behavior: Copying host bytes to an accelerator pointer selects the matching device, switches to its device ordinal, performs a host-to-device copy, and preserves the bytes.
entries.reason: Rust FFI exposes copy_from_host but has no discoverable fake-device test for device selection, context switching, copy direction, and byte preservation.

entries.behavior: Copying from an accelerator pointer to host selects the matching device, switches to its device ordinal, performs a device-to-host copy, and preserves the bytes.
entries.reason: Rust FFI exposes copy_to_host but has no discoverable fake-device test for device selection, context switching, copy direction, and byte preservation.

entries.behavior: Pointer classification returns the accelerator device whose query reports device memory and preserves the reported device ordinal.
entries.reason: Rust tests raw pointer-kind enum decoding but not runtime device selection or preservation of a matching device ordinal.

entries.behavior: A null pointer is rejected before querying any accelerator device.
entries.reason: Rust classify_pointer delegates directly to native code and has no discoverable test proving null is rejected without a native device query.

entries.behavior: Adding and removing keys from the LRU policy updates its visible candidate count.
entries.reason: Rust tests LRU victim ordering but has no direct candidate lifecycle/count test equivalent to add, remove, and cleanup.

entries.behavior: LRU eviction returns the least recently used key first and moves updated keys behind untouched newer candidates.
The C++ FIFO policy keeps randomly removed keys in its internal lazy queue and reports the unchanged queue size until eviction cleanup.
entries.reason: C++ tests a lazy-queue implementation detail. Rust couples FIFO entries to its storage index and removes deleted records eagerly; externally visible deletion and eviction correctness are covered separately.

entries.behavior: FIFO eviction returns the oldest inserted key and key updates do not reorder later FIFO victims.
The C++ generic ThreadPool executes all enqueued tasks.
entries.reason: Rust Store uses Tokio and component-owned workers rather than the C++ ThreadPool class; this internal class contract is outside the Rust product boundary.

review.oracle: mooncake-store/tests/thread_pool_test.cpp and the C++ ThreadPool class

entries.behavior: The C++ generic ThreadPool bounds concurrent task execution by its configured worker count.
entries.reason: Rust Store uses Tokio and component-owned workers rather than the C++ ThreadPool class; this internal scheduler implementation is outside the Rust product boundary.

entries.behavior: Stopping the C++ generic ThreadPool waits for accepted work and rejects later enqueue attempts.
entries.reason: Rust Store has component-specific shutdown contracts rather than the C++ ThreadPool class; its enqueue-after-stop exception is not a Rust Store API.

review.oracle: mooncake-store/tests/thread_pool_test.cpp and the C++ ThreadPool class

entries.behavior: The C++ generic ThreadPool completes a stress batch of one thousand tasks without loss.
entries.reason: Rust Store does not use the C++ ThreadPool class; workload and fault tests cover its Tokio/component worker behavior at product boundaries.

entries.behavior: An RPC deadline failure has a dedicated timeout error class, distinct from generic service failure, with a human-readable timeout message.
A configured short RPC timeout bounds an unanswered readiness call and reports timeout rather than generic RPC failure.
entries.reason: Rust separately tests timeout configuration parsing and deadline status mapping, but has no black-hole server test proving an actual RPC honors the configured wall-clock budget.

entries.behavior: Republishing byte-identical RPC metadata is idempotent and leaves the original metadata available.
Republishing changed RPC metadata for an existing location is rejected and does not overwrite the original value.
Starting the HTTP metadata listener on an occupied address reports bind failure.
A CXL-backed client can put and get an object with exact byte preservation.
entries.reason: Rust tests CXL configuration and placement selection but has no end-to-end CXL put/get byte-integrity test.

entries.behavior: A CXL-backed client supports batch put and get while preserving every object's bytes.
entries.reason: Rust has no end-to-end CXL batch put/get integrity test.

entries.behavior: Evicting a CXL-backed object removes it from the client-visible data path.
entries.reason: Rust has no end-to-end CXL eviction test.

entries.behavior: Snapshot-only standby startup restores configured snapshot metadata, discards stale state, and exposes the restored sequence as applied progress.
Snapshot-only standby startup with no available snapshot succeeds from an empty metadata and sequence baseline.
If standby startup fails due to invalid snapshot configuration, promotion returns the same failure instead of hiding it.
An empty tenant identifier normalizes to the canonical default tenant while named tenants retain their value and default classification.
Canonical tenant validation accepts default and ordinary names while rejecting the reserved underscore prefix and control bytes.
Tenant identifiers provide stable lexical ordering and hash-key equality.
A scoped key preserves colons and path characters and round-trips by splitting only at the tenant/local-key NUL delimiter.
Scoped-key parsing preserves embedded NUL bytes in the local key after the first tenant delimiter.
A legacy key without a tenant delimiter parses as belonging to the default tenant without changing the local key.
A Unix-domain IPC connection transfers an exact raw request and response payload in both directions.
Unix-domain IPC transfers an SCM_RIGHTS file descriptor from the initiating endpoint and the receiver can use the same underlying file.
Receiving an SCM_RIGHTS descriptor with a shorter-than-required payload fails and closes the received descriptor.
Unix-domain IPC transfers an SCM_RIGHTS file descriptor from the accepting endpoint and the initiator can use the same underlying file.
Stopping the C++ background UDS acceptor wakes its accept loop and removes the listening endpoint.
entries.reason: Rust Dummy IPC exposes a caller-owned one-shot listener rather than the C++ background UdsAcceptor, so this internal accept-loop lifecycle is not a Rust API contract.

entries.behavior: Stopping the C++ background UDS acceptor shuts down active connections so blocked handlers wake and exit.
entries.reason: Rust Dummy IPC does not own a background acceptor or handler threads; connection and thread cancellation remain with its caller.

entries.behavior: A Unix-domain connector rejects a non-positive connection timeout before attempting to connect.
entries.reason: Rust DummyIpcChannel has no configurable connect-timeout parameter or validation contract.

entries.behavior: Connecting to a missing Unix-domain endpoint with a short timeout fails promptly and identifies the endpoint.
entries.reason: Rust uses blocking UnixStream::connect without an explicit timeout budget and has no prompt-failure/error-context test.

entries.behavior: After a timed Unix-domain connect succeeds, the connector clears its temporary socket send timeout.
entries.reason: Rust UnixStream::connect does not install a temporary SO_SNDTIMEO, so clearing that C++ implementation detail is not applicable.

entries.behavior: Starting the C++ background UDS acceptor without a registered handler fails with an explicit handler error.
entries.reason: Rust Dummy IPC exposes no handler-registration or background acceptor API; callers invoke the one-shot listener and process the returned channel directly.
